precepts.text: I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee: Christ, not Joshua, fulfilled this word.
precepts.point: None matched all the signs and the wonders which the Lord sent Moses to do in the land of Egypt, and all that mighty hand, and all the great terror which Moses shewed in the sight of all Israel. With this the Torah, the books of Moses, is finished.
precepts.why:
“I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him.” This is what makes Deuteronomy 34:10 heavy, because of a doctrine: some say Joshua was the prophet raised up like unto Moses, and therefore there is no Christ.

But the scripture that acknowledges Joshua rising up with the spirit upon him says in the same breath, “there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face”. Joshua was a mighty prophet, but he did not fit that word. None matched “all the signs and the wonders, which the Lord sent him to do in the land of Egypt”, “all that mighty hand”, and “all the great terror which Moses shewed in the sight of all Israel.”

Christ did. Christ, not Joshua, fulfilled this word: the Prophet like unto Moses, with the words of the Most High put in his mouth, speaking all that he was commanded. With this the Torah, the books of Moses, is finished.

precepts.text: Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.
precepts.point: The same way we make haste to stop the different sins, be quick to change the diet. If we make haste to change those things, the Most High will also keep away that continual sickness, the diabetes and everything causing our limbs to be cut off just to live.

note.label: Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High

precepts.why:
Caleb at fourscore and five is “as strong this day as I was in the day that Moses sent me”, an eighty-five-year-old man in perfect health. Moses was the same way: “And Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.” A hundred and twenty years old with the strength and the vision of a young man.

A lot of us are not living to a hundred and twenty, but at the same time we are making it to sixty and seventy, and at fifty we are hooked up on machines. We are all going to die at some point, but that does not mean you have to be miserable, sitting there hooked up to all kind of machines while you are here.

precepts.text: Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom, but "there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face," so the prophet like Moses is not Joshua.
precepts.point: "Like unto thee," like unto Moses, means the same similarities: Moses spoke to the Most High directly, mediated between the Most High and Israel, gave the laws, was hidden as a child when the young were sought to be killed, and led Israel toward the promised land.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
Some would say the prophet like Moses was Joshua: “And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the Lord commanded Moses.”

But read on, and there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face. Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom, but he was not that prophet. The prophet like unto Moses was still to come.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 21 Thy Kingdom Come

precepts.why: Read by the other speaker. “Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died”: that’s a long time. “His eye was not dim”: at 120, your eyes usually start to get small; old age catches up on you, but that didn’t happen to Moses. “Nor his natural force abated”: it didn’t leave him. He wasn’t weak and feeble and shaking; you couldn’t test him. And that wasn’t even the kingdom yet; the Lord was dealing with Moses on a different level.

points: Moses went up from the plains of Moab unto the mountain of Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, over against Jericho, and the Most High shewed him all the land: Gilead unto Dan, Naphtali, Ephraim and Manasseh, Judah unto the utmost sea, the south, and the plain of the valley of Jericho unto Zoar.

This is the land which I sware unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, saying, I will give it unto thy seed: I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither. Moses could see it, but he could not go into it.

So Moses the servant of the Lord died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the Lord, and he was buried in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Bethpeor: but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day. So do not go trying to find it.

Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated. He was not weak, old, and sickly like a man about to drop dead; he was in full strength, and still he had to go up and die because he could not enter the land.
The children of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days, until the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were ended.

Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him. Joshua was Moses' protege, and he carried the spirit Moses had, a great leader compassionate for the people; and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the Lord commanded Moses.

And there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face. This verse is heavy because of a doctrine: some say Joshua was the prophet of Deuteronomy 18:18, the prophet raised up like unto Moses, and therefore there is no Christ.

But the scripture that acknowledges Joshua rising up with the spirit upon him says in the same breath that there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses. Joshua was a mighty prophet, but he did not fit that word; Christ did.

None matched all the signs and the wonders which the Lord sent Moses to do in the land of Egypt, and all that mighty hand, and all the great terror which Moses shewed in the sight of all Israel. With this the Torah, the books of Moses, is finished.
